I've played the beta on both PC and XBox One. I'm a PC gamer 100% and the beta runs MUCH better on the XBox than the PC. It seems designed exclusively for consoles, which is NOT good.

I've been playing DOOM I & II since both were released. I've consistently had the games installed on every PC I've ever owned. I know DOOM, I love DOOM, and I wanted this new game to be awesome.

It is horrible in every way imaginable. There is nothing even slightly DOOM-like about it. Nothing. The marine doesn't bob or grunt. You can only carry 2 weapons and the game forces loadouts. The double-jumping is foreign to the series. The focus on multi-player as the first reveal is ill-considered. The gameplay is absolutely pedestrian and comes off as a poor copy of Unreal Tournament or Halo. If this game reflects any id lineage, I would only agree that it is to Quake Arena. Certainly not DOOM.

For the life of me I cannot understand why anyone would think this game design was appropriate for DOOM. You'd think they would have learned their lesson from DOOM 3 which, although it has some fans, received so much criticism for straying from the original DOOM design elements.

I am glad they released the open beta because I had planned on pre-ordering the game and now will not. I suppose I'll try and keep an open mind and wait for reviews of the single-player campaign, but the inclusion of so many console elements and DLC is revolting to me. Ultimately, it might find a home in my gaming library when a Steam sale comes along offering it for less than $10.

This is truly the greatest let-down in classic gaming reboots since Duke Nukem Forever. The open beta reveals that the new "DOOM" is far, far worse than DNF which at least made (failing) attempts to recapture the humor of the original. This new game is not DOOM by any standard other than that the developers purchased the right to name it as such. There is only one studio that I believe is competent to produce a worthy DOOM sequel, and that is Croteam, the creators of Serious Sam. They understand run & gun gameplay design and have successfully employed it in multiple iterations of their releases. This new "DOOM" is built by & for console gamers, and it condescends to them by giving them a mish-mash of Halo meets CoD meets UT instead of staying true to the intellectual property that made DOOM the first and greatest FPS of all time.

What you said.

It drives me nuts. It's easy as hell to imagine what a new Doom should be like but the devs go in a completely different direction every dam time. Console players will probably enjoy this game, but the only way I'm going to buy it is if they release full mod tools so the PC fans can fix all the console cuckery.

"Going back to their roots" my ass.

I sat and listened to the dev's presentations about the new game. They seemed earnest about wanting to stay true to the original design elements, however the videos they were demoing and discussing just didn't show any evidence of the words they were mouthing. This open beta clearly reveals that this game's only interest in DOOM is to capitalize on the name. There are literally zero similarities to the original franchise. Zero. Although the single-player campaign will have you battling imps and cacodemons, I'm pretty confident we can now conclude that the developer's interest in the DOOM franchise was as a money grab and not to deliver an authentic, worthy sequel.

Now that they've revealed that the new game will be "pay to win" and have DLC, I'm seriously questioning their commitment to supporting a mod community. The sole reason that people still play DOOM today is that id actively encouraged modding and eventually gave away the engine. Since this new game seems more focused on consoles and they're going to be (trying to) sell DLC, I wouldn't hold my breath for meaningful mod tools. And even if such tools are made available, the game looks likely to tank so interest in modding won't be as great so the quantity and quality of mods is likely to be low.

I wish I had something more positive to say, but I have seen absolutely nothing to give me hope.
